# Core-Geth

> Core-Geth is the Ethereum Classic execution client, maintained at
> [github.com/ethereumclassic/core-geth](https://github.com/ethereumclassic/core-geth) in the Ethereum Classic
> community's GitHub organization. It is a go-ethereum downstream that holds chain configuration as data, so one
> binary serves Ethereum Classic, the Mordor test network, MintMe and private chains. The current release is
> `v1.13.0`, published 14 September 2026.

Releases are published from `ethereumclassic/core-geth`. Archives published under the previous `etclabscore`
namespace are not built from this source. The ETC Cooperative board has communicated its intent to archive
`etclabscore/core-geth`.

## Start here

- [Node operators: start here](https://docs.coregeth.com/operators/): the short path for node, pool, exchange and RPC operators: what to do now, and what to read in what order.
- [Documentation home](https://docs.coregeth.com/): what this client is, which networks it supports, and where to go first.
- [Installation](https://docs.coregeth.com/getting-started/installation/): download, checksum and install a release.
- [Running a node](https://docs.coregeth.com/getting-started/run-a-node/): Linux, macOS, Windows and Docker, with the flags each kind of node needs.
- [Upgrading to v1.13.0](https://docs.coregeth.com/tutorials/v1.13.0-migration/): the upgrade path from the `v1.12.x` line, including the required node key rotation.

## What this project is

- [Project history](https://docs.coregeth.com/about/project-history/): the lineage of the code, from go-ethereum through multi-geth, and of the organizations that funded and maintained it from 2018 to today.
- [Questions and answers](https://docs.coregeth.com/about/faq/): which repository publishes releases, which version to run, why node key rotation is required, MESS, public RPC endpoints and how to verify a download.
- [Support this work](https://docs.coregeth.com/support/): how this client's maintenance is funded, who depends on it, and the routes for sponsoring it.

## Security and provenance

- [v1.13.0 release report](https://docs.coregeth.com/release-reports/v1.13.0/): what the release fixes, what it changes, and how to verify a download.
- [v1.13.0: the record behind the release](https://docs.coregeth.com/release-reports/v1.13.0-record/): claims made about this release after it shipped, answered from commit metadata, pull requests, release files and advisory records.
- [March 2026 security audit](https://docs.coregeth.com/audits/2026-03-security-audit/): six CVEs and a GraphQL denial of service in the `v1.12.x` line, with the per-release breakdown and the disclosure timeline.
- [August 2026 security follow-up](https://docs.coregeth.com/audits/2026-08-security-followup/): `v1.12.23` measured at its tag against the advisory records.
- [Go toolchain](https://docs.coregeth.com/audits/2026-09-go-toolchain/): which Go toolchain built each published archive, and the standard library advisories each one carries.
- [Dependency and toolchain modernization](https://docs.coregeth.com/audits/2026-08-dependency-modernization/): what changed underneath the code between the December 2024 archive point and `v1.13.0`.
- [Release artifacts](https://docs.coregeth.com/audits/2026-09-release-pipeline/): what the published archives actually contain, measured rather than inferred from the build configuration.

## The network and its services

- [The ETC Cooperative transition](https://docs.coregeth.com/etc-cooperative-transition/): where the services the ETC Cooperative maintained continue as it winds down, including the public JSON-RPC endpoints and the peer discovery lists.
- [Bootnodes and peer discovery](https://docs.coregeth.com/guides/bootnodes-and-discovery/): how the discovery trees are built from a crawl of the network, and how to point a node at any other list.
- [MESS](https://docs.coregeth.com/operate/mess/): what ECBP-1100 does, why this release ships it on by default, and how to turn it off.

## Operating a node

- [Security and network exposure](https://docs.coregeth.com/operate/security/): which ports and APIs to expose, and which to keep closed.
- [Sync modes and data retention](https://docs.coregeth.com/operate/sync-modes/): what each sync mode stores and what it costs.
- [Maintenance, backup and upgrades](https://docs.coregeth.com/operate/maintenance/): keeping a node healthy over time.
- [Public RPC endpoint](https://docs.coregeth.com/guides/public-rpc-endpoint/): serving JSON-RPC to other people from your own node.
- [Endpoints for your own project](https://docs.coregeth.com/guides/developer-endpoints/): running your own JSON-RPC and archive endpoints for an application you are building, and getting Mordor test coins by mining rather than from a faucet.
- [Mining](https://docs.coregeth.com/guides/mining/) and [mining pool node](https://docs.coregeth.com/guides/mining-pool-node/): what a pool's node needs.

## Building and developing

- [Build from source](https://docs.coregeth.com/developers/build-from-source/): the Go version required and the build commands.
- [JSON-RPC API](https://docs.coregeth.com/JSON-RPC-API/): the methods this client serves, by module.
- [Cutting a release](https://docs.coregeth.com/developers/create-new-release/): how a release is built and published.
